strategy.summary: The shop serves four pages (/, /cart, /about, /contact, as listed in server.js and /sitemap.xml). This adds @axe-core/playwright scans (already a devDependency) to the Playwright e2e suite. Pages with no critical/serious WCAG 2.x A/AA violations get a passing scan. Pages that have them (/cart: images with no alt; /about: #c7c7c7 small print) keep the same assertion, marked test.fail and recorded as defects. Revision 2: each of those pages also gets a passing test that pins its known violations exactly, so a page that stops loading, or a new violation, fails the suite instead of being absorbed by test.fail. A sitemap check makes sure a new page can't go unscanned.
inScope: axe scan of each of the four pages on load
axe scan of the contact page after sending a message (DOM changes: status message)
pinning the exact known violations on the failing pages
check that the scanned pages are exactly the pages the sitemap lists
outOfScope: Fixing the violations in public/*.html (application source)
Manual keyboard / screen-reader checks (axe cannot prove them)
assumptions: The real server (node server.js) runs for every test via the existing playwright webServer; nothing is faked.
Blocking = axe impact critical or serious under tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa; moderate/minor violations are attached to the test report, not failed on.

'Report the violations on the others' means: keep the failing scan as a test.fail expected failure (its failure output lists rule id, impact and targets), record each as a defect, and pin the known violations in a passing test that must be updated when they are fixed.
openQuestions: The cart page after applying a coupon is not scanned separately: the whole-page scan already fails on the images, and scoping the scan would need a CSS selector (the coupon form has no accessible name). Worth adding once /cart is fixed.

risks.description: test.fail passes on any failure, so an expected-failure scan could hide a different breakage
risks.mitigation: TC8/TC9 pin the exact known violations in passing tests

risks.description: A new page is added without a scan
risks.mitigation: TC7 compares the sitemap with the scanned paths

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every page of the shop is scanned with axe in the e2e tests, and the pages without critical/serious violations pass the scan
Pages with critical/serious violations have a scan that reports the violations (rule id, impact, offending elements) and is tracked as a known failure rather than skipped
A page state that changes the DOM after interaction (contact form sent) is scanned too

defects.title: Cart page product images have no alt text (axe image-alt, critical)
defects.description: AC1/AC2: /cart should have no critical/serious WCAG A/AA violations. The two elements in public/cart.html have no alt attribute, so axe reports image-alt (critical, WCAG 1.1.1). Test is marked test.fail().
defects.evidence: public/cart.html lines 19-20: without alt; the scan's toEqual([]) fails (test.fail passes).

defects.title: About page small print fails colour contrast (axe color-contrast, serious)
defects.description: AC1/AC2: /about should have no critical/serious WCAG AA violations. The .small-print paragraph is #c7c7c7 on #ffffff (about 1.7:1, below 4.5:1), so axe reports color-contrast (serious, WCAG 1.4.3). Test is marked test.fail().
defects.evidence: public/about.html lines 7-10 and 25; the scan's toEqual([]) fails (test.fail passes).

review.standard: General test automation standards / Playwright rules: a known defect is kept as an expected failure without the assertion passing for the wrong reason (strategy risk: 'an expected-failure scan could hide a different breakage')
review.summary: `test.fail()` covers the whole cart test (and the about test at line 81), so it passes on any failure, including the page not loading or a different blocking violation, and nothing in the test pins the expected one (image-alt on the two cart images, color-contrast on the about small print).
review.failureScenario:
Say /cart starts returning 404, or `

Your cart

` is renamed. The heading assertion on line 70 fails, and because of `test.fail()` the test still passes and shows as an expected failure. The same happens if someone fixes the missing alt text but adds a new critical violation (for example a button with no accessible name): the expected failure still holds, so the new violation is never reported. The about test (lines 81-88) has the same problem with color-contrast. Fix: keep the `toEqual([])` expected-failure assertion, and also check which violations come back, for example `expect(violations.map(v => v.id)).toEqual(['image-alt'])` with the two image targets, in a test that is expected to pass. Then a page that stops loading, or a violation that changes, fails the suite.

review.standard: General test automation standards: assert meaningful outcomes (TC7: 'fails when a page is added without a scan')
review.summary: `SCANNED_PATHS` is a hand-written list that nothing ties to the scan tests (each test hard-codes its own `page.goto`), so the sitemap test proves the sitemap matches this list, not that every listed page is scanned.
review.failureScenario: Someone adds `/faq` to `pages` in server.js. The sitemap test fails as intended, but they make it pass by adding '/faq' to `SCANNED_PATHS` and write no scan test, so /faq goes unscanned while TC7 stays green. Generating the per-page load scans from `SCANNED_PATHS`, with a heading and expected-failure entry for each page, would tie the two together.

review.standard: General test automation standards: TestForge rule 'Assert the one outcome the app produces'; the accepted strategy's TC9/TC8 expected results (the small-print paragraph; the two product images)
review.summary: The pin tests only check each violation's rule id, impact and number of elements (`elements: targets.length`). They never check which elements are flagged, so a known violation can be fixed while the same rule fails on another element, and the tests still pass.
review.failureScenario: Someone fixes the small print in public/about.html (for example by setting `.small-print` to #595959) and, in the same change, gives the intro paragraph on line 24 a light grey colour. axe still reports exactly one serious color-contrast node, now on the intro paragraph instead of `.small-print`. TC9 (line 116) still passes and TC5 still fails as expected, so the suite stays green: the new violation is absorbed and the fix isn't noticed. The strategy says this pin exists to prevent exactly that. The cart pin at line 103 has the same gap: if the two product images get alt text but two other images without alt are added, it still sees `{ image-alt, critical, 2 }`. Fix: assert the targets too, e.g. `toEqual([{ id: 'color-contrast', impact: 'serious', targets: ['.small-print'] }])`, and for /cart the two product image targets axe reports (or check each node's `html` for the product image).
